launches.title: Social AI: Put E-commerce Social Media on Autopilot
launches.tagline: Safely automate social media moderation across Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok.
launches.detail_body:
👋 We are Yuma, YC W23. Since 2023, we've automated over 5 million customer interactions for leading e-commerce brands with Support AI and Sales AI. Today we're launching our newest product: **Social AI**

Social AI puts your brand's social media comments on autopilot. It connects to your Facebook, Instagram, and soon TikTok pages, ingests every comment in real time, classifies each one by intent and sentiment, and acts based on automation rules you define. In early testing, Social AI safely automates up to 60% of repetitive social media moderation.

**Why this matters**: because social comments are one of the last unmanaged channels in e-commerce. They're public, they shape brand perception, and most teams have no system for handling them. And "safely" matters here. One careless AI reply on a post can reach thousands of eyes in minutes.

**Why we built it**

We kept hearing the same thing from customer support and social teams at high-growth brands: social comments are a blind spot.

* "A negative comment sits on a post for days and nobody can catch it."
* "Someone asked a product question under our Instagram ad. By the time we saw it, they'd already bought from a competitor."
* "A frustrated customer tagged us publicly. It snowballed into 40+ replies before anyone on our team even noticed."
* "A customer leaves a glowing comment and we don't even say thank you."
* "We have 1 person manually scrolling through hundreds of comments."

Support tickets have tools. Social comments didn't. We've been running Social AI in private beta for the past year. Today, after a major upgrade, we're opening it up to everyone.

**What's different**

* Works across both paid and organic posts. Negative comments on your ads are conversion killers, and Social AI catches them before they cost you.
* Built-in automation templates for common scenarios (reply, like, hide, flag, or skip), with the ability to create fully custom rules
* Configurable agent persona: set the tone, verbosity, and brand guidelines so replies sound like your team wrote them
* Advanced targeting based on the commenter's follower count, so high-profile users get the extra care they deserve
* Crisis prevention: automatically detect and escalate comments that could spiral into bigger brand issues before they do
* 24/7 coverage. 50% of comments are posted outside business hours and on weekends. Social AI is always on so your brand is never unprotected.
* Safety first: every automation rule is scoped by platform, intent, sentiment, and user popularity. You stay in control of what gets automated and what doesn't
* Real-time dashboard with engagements, automation coverage, sentiment distribution, negative exposure rate, and unanswered rate across all platforms

**The demo video:**

<https://youtu.be/6X6W_k6Cs8c>

**Looking for:**

Are you running an e-commerce brand and leaving social comments unmanaged? We'd love to help you set up Social AI, configure your automations, and track the impact with a 30-day free trial. 👀

Contact Guillaume, the founder at [g-social-ai-launch@yuma.ai](mailto:g-social-ai-launch@yuma.ai) for priority setup.

**What else does Yuma do?**

We also offer AI agents for e-commerce support (Support AI) and a product page Q&A widget to boost conversion (Sales AI). On top of that, our platform includes a visual automation builder (Flows) and a ChatGPT-like interface for surfacing customer voice insights from support tickets (Deep Search). :)

launches.title: Cajal: Scaling Formal Verification for Scientific Discovery
launches.tagline: Cajal deploys AI mathematicians to high-impact applied domains, starting with quantum computing and finance.
launches.detail_body:
**TL;DR: Formal verification** uses mathematical proofs to guarantee a system behaves as intended.  Cajal is **massively scaling this technology** with AI - deploying agents to autonomously discover and **formalize new tools** across applied mathematics with genuine real world impact. Starting with **quantum computing and finance.**\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7McsRwyWBNE>

**LLMs: The State of Play**

Large language models are fundamentally stochastic. No amount of scaling changes this - probabilistic systems cannot guarantee correctness. This is especially problematic in mission-critical domains that require mathematical certainty.

Formal verification provides exactly this: mathematical proof that code is correct for every possible input, not just the ones you test. 

Previously, this technology has been limited to a small group of experts working over long horizons - restricting its application to narrow domains like software verification and research mathematics.

**A New Frontier for Formal Verification**

Cajal is using AI to massively scale this technology - deploying agents to autonomously discover and formalize tools across applied science, beginning with quantum computing and finance.

**Introducing Tau:** Tau is a multi-agent system that collaborates to discover and verify new mathematical proofs in Lean. Given a research direction, Tau autonomously formalizes large corpora of applied mathematics, discovering novel results with real-world applications - from algorithms with certified speedups to certificates that a system satisfies its constraints.

Every result is machine-verified by Lean's type-checking kernel, guaranteeing correctness.

**Our Ask**\
Alongside our work formalizing applied mathematics, we also partner with frontier AI labs and research institutes to improve their systems, including through datasets, evals, and RL environments. To explore a collaboration, contact us at [hi@caj.al](mailto:hi@caj.al).

→ [Luke](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lukerjohnston/) and [Pedro](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pedronobree/) from [Cajal](https://caj.al/)

launches.title: Pluto - Commoditizing Compute
launches.tagline: The regulated derivatives exchange for AI infrastructure
launches.detail_body:
**Compute is the new oil.**

GPU and memory pricing can move **20–40%** in months, while startups, chipmakers, and infrastructure providers remain structurally exposed to volatility. Unlike traditional commodities, compute has no forward curve, no standardized hedge, and no benchmark contracts to support the trillions in AI capital expenditures expected over the next decade.

### What we’re building

Pluto is building a CFTC-regulated commodities exchange for AI infrastructure.

We treat compute and memory like commodities, beginning with standardized GPU contracts (H100, A100, B200, and successors) and expanding into other critical AI inputs such as power and rare earth metals.

Our applications have been submitted and deemed **materially complete** by the CFTC for both an exchange ([PMEX Markets](https://www.cftc.gov/IndustryOversight/IndustryFilings/TradingOrganizations)) and clearinghouse ([PMEX Clearing](https://www.cftc.gov/IndustryOversight/IndustryFilings/ClearingOrganizations)).

Upon approval, Pluto would operate with the same regulatory framework that governs major U.S. futures exchanges.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98145&key=user_uploads/1526382/98fa6337-82ae-4b99-bdad-53055c765121)

### Why this matters

Obtaining DCM and DCO approval is a high-bar regulatory process that few new entrants pursue. By choosing a regulatory-focused approach from the beginning, Pluto will be the first to launch a regulated marketplace for compute derivatives.

In commodity markets, the exchange that establishes the initial benchmark contract and forward curve typically anchors liquidity and price discovery. Early regulatory approval creates a sequencing advantage: the first regulated venue to list and clear these contracts sets the standard others reference.

By combining regulatory infrastructure with proprietary benchmark construction, Pluto is establishing the compute forward curve before the market fully commoditizes.

### Who we are

Pluto was founded by Ronit and Aarav, who met at UC Berkeley’s Sky Computing Lab researching GPU optimization and large-scale compute systems.

Our team combines deep technical and market-structure experience, including former staff engineers from Meta and NVIDIA, EE PhDs, and the former CFO of ElectronX.

Our public directors bring direct exchange and regulatory expertise: Rich Jaycobs (formerly of Cantor Exchange, involved in numerous DCM/DCO approvals) and Andrew Ridenour (former General Counsel at Cumberland Labs).

### Our Asks

We’re looking to connect with:

• Funds focused on financial infrastructure, commodities, or AI\
• Market makers interested in participating in compute derivatives\
• AI companies with meaningful GPU spend interested in hedging\
• Data centers and neoclouds exposed to GPU price volatility

If you’re building or investing in the financial layer of AI, please book a time [here](https://pluto.trade).

launches.title: Confluence Labs: an AI research lab focused on learning efficiency
launches.tagline: an AI research lab focused on learning efficiency
launches.detail_body:
Confluence Labs is coming out of stealth with **SOTA on ARC-AGI-2** with a score of **97.9%** at $11.77 per task on the public eval. This is how we did it, why it matters, and what's next.

ARC-AGI-2 is a benchmark that tests an AI system's ability to solve novel reasoning tasks from just a few examples. It's considered one of the hardest AI benchmarks in the world. As recently as a year ago, even the best models scored in the single digits.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98111&key=user_uploads/1164255/2f4e4c89-6f96-48ca-93ea-a84eccc15092)

We've open sourced our SOTA solver. You can reproduce our results here: <https://github.com/confluence-labs/arc-agi-2>.

**Our Approach – Program Synthesis driven by LLMs**

LLMs are exceedingly good at writing code. We take the latest models and allow them to find the optimal solution by directing them to write code which describes the transformation represented by a particular ARC problem.

The principles of our approach can be boiled down to a few key ideas:

1\. Structure the problem such that it optimally resembles the underlying LLM's training data

2\. Enable long-horizon work on the problem so a model can continue to build on its past work

3\. Precisely structure the criteria of the solution and give the model a way to measure that

**ARC-AGI-2 is Saturated – What Does This Mean for the World?**

ARC is a data efficiency benchmark. It measures how well you can make a prediction based on a few examples. Typical approaches to ARC-AGI have struggled because modern ML excels in areas where you can collect a lot of training data, but struggles in areas where data is sparse or costly to attain.

We think LLMs can be used in combination with discrete modeling to assist humans in data-sparse domains. We're most excited about the application of this to meaningful and challenging frontiers such as hardware engineering, drug design, and physics research.

**What Does This Mean for Us?**

Our core belief is that learning efficiency is the key bottleneck to solving the world's hardest problems. We think AI can help in data-sparse domains, and we're approaching this from 2 angles:

1\. **Hypothesis generation** – A hypothesis is a testable prediction about the world. If you optimally generate hypotheses, the results of your experiments are maximally informative, and you can reduce the time it takes to develop a new technology or solve a hard problem.

2\. **Data-Efficient Modeling** – By pushing the capabilities of both LLMs and discrete program search, we can make predictions with far less data and accelerate frontier research.

**What's Next?**

We're going hard on developing our core technology, building out the team, and developing partnerships with researchers and engineers. We're looking for collaborators in hardware engineering, biology, materials science, and other fields where progress is gated by the cost of physical experiments. If that sounds like you or someone you know, reach out at [founders@confluence.sh](mailto:founders@confluence.sh).

launches.title: Docura Health - AI-Native Med-Legal Firm to automate tedious workers’ comp workflows for doctors
launches.tagline: Turn thousands of pages of medical records into draft-ready reports in minutes.
launches.detail_body:
**Problem:**

When a worker gets injured on the job, they see their primary doctor for treatment. The doctor treats them through a series of appointments until they reach maximum medical improvement - the point where no more treatment will improve their condition.

If the insurance company denies the claim, that's when the bottleneck kicks in. Both sides get attorneys, and they send all the medical records to a Qualified Medical Evaluator (QME) for an independent assessment.

The QME has to manually review these records. Some cases have thousands of pages, while others have tens of thousands. Even straightforward cases take 6-8 hours. Complex cases can take multiple days.

There are also agencies that take 40% of the revenue per case to do some of this administrative work for them.

Either way, doctors are missing out. They're either losing significant revenue to agencies, or they're spending so much time on paperwork that they can't handle more cases.

**Solution:**

Docura Health automates the entire workflow:

Upload medical record PDFs and case documents → we generate fully compliant record reviews and reports in 30 minutes

Automate patient history collection calls that admin staff normally handle before evaluations

Doctors handle significantly more cases while keeping far more revenue per case.

\*\*Demo Video:\*\*\
<https://youtu.be/y2CU0QIXSS4>

**Progress:**

We’re live with multiple healthcare practices and med-legal expert groups. Providers working with us have doubled their case volume from the last month and some even process over 50k pages per month.

**Ask From YC:**

* If anyone knows any qualified medical evaluators or independent medical evaluators that are orthopedic surgeons, pain medicine doctors, or internal medicine doctors, would appreciate warm intros.
* If anyone knows any med-legal expert groups or lawyers on both the defense and the applicant side, would also appreciate intros.

launches.title: Sureform: Turning physical expertise into training data for world models and robotics
launches.tagline: Building the platform to acquire task-specific robotics data at scale
launches.detail_body:
Sureform connects workplaces like hotels, warehouses, and restaurants with robotics labs to collect task-specific training data for world models and robot foundation models.

**Problem**

To create a future where robots can reliably perform specialized tasks, like restocking inventory in a pharmacy or repairing downed power lines, robotics teams need massive amounts of task-specific human and robot data. Data that’s crafted in simulation or in controlled environments doesn’t reflect the natural variation and complexity of the world, and as a result, we need significantly more real-world action data across each of the millions of highly-specialized physical tasks that need to be automated.

**Solution**

To solve this problem, Sureform’s platform enable robotics teams to get task-specific data from workplaces like hotels, construction sites, laundromats, and warehouses, where employees are equipped with head-mounted RGB cameras, stereo depth rigs, and handheld grippers that capture time-synced video, audio, pose, depth, and tactile data as they work. Every session of data captured through our platform is structured, synchronized, and delivered training-ready.

\

launches.title: Proliferate: the open source company coding agent
launches.tagline: Build yourself an AI coworker that actually takes work off your plate
launches.detail_body:
**TL;DR:** Local coding agents can't do real end-to-end work at your company. Proliferate is the open-source, self-hostable platform for building company-specific background agents that can. Agents get their own sandboxes with secure access to your internal services, trigger from any event, and expose a live, multiplayer preview so your team can verify the work together. MIT licensed.

**Star the repo:** <https://github.com/proliferate-ai/proliferate>

**Get started self-hosting:** <https://docs.proliferate.com/>

**Sign up for self-serve waitlist:** <https://proliferate.com/waitlist>

**The Problem**

Coding agents today hit a wall the second they need to do real work. Fixing an actual bug means querying your staging database, reading internal Datadog logs, hitting proprietary APIs. You can't hand those keys to a generic cloud SaaS agent.

So you run agents locally. But that ties up your machine, forces you to babysit a terminal, and traps all the context on your laptop where nobody else can see it.

The most forward-looking engineering orgs- Stripe, Ramp, coinbase- spent months building custom infrastructure to solve this. Some are now merging 50+% of their PRs with agents.

Proliferate open-sources that infrastructure so every team can do the same.

**What teams use Proliferate for:**

* **On-call triage:** Sentry exception fires → agent reproduces the issue in a cloud sandbox → writes a fix → shares a live preview link in Slack for the team to verify.
* **Flaky test sweeps:** Cron job runs overnight → agent isolates flaky CI tests by running them 1,000x → PR is waiting by morning.
* **Mass migrations:** Bump React versions or internal API contracts across 50 microservices and fix the resulting breaking changes- automatically.
* **Team verification:** Agent gets a feature 80% done. Instead of reading the diff, the team clicks a live preview URL. A developer jumps into the shared terminal to fix the last failing test. Feature is merged.

**Demo: [https://youtu.be/H84HrOJx4QM](https://youtu.be/H84HrOJx4QM)**

**What makes it different**

Every agent gets its own sandbox with your Docker containers running, secure access to your internal services via our action catalog, and can be configured to respond to any trigger. Your code and data stay in your control- fully self-hostable, MIT licensed.

Another large difference comes with how your team interacts with the work. Reading AI-generated code is tedious. So every session produces a live UR. Sessions are multiplayer. Anyone on the team can jump in, check logs, or steer the agent in real-time.

**Our ask:** ⭐ Star the repo- we just open-sourced it. <https://github.com/proliferate-ai/proliferate>

If you're tired of handholding local agents and want to move them to the background with real infrastructure access, reach out. We're working closely with a handful of teams to help improve their engineering velocity and adoption of AI. [Book a demo](https://cal.com/team/proliferate/demo) or email [pablo@proliferate.com](mailto:pablo@proliferate.com).

launches.title: Radars for end-to-end autonomy
launches.tagline: The radar to unlock mass-market self-driving cars
launches.detail_body:
**TL;DR:** Everyone wants an autonomous car, but today they are cost prohibitive because they rely on multiple lidars. The answer is radar, it's tens of dollars, already in most cars, and works in all weather. The problem: no one has built a radar compatible with end-to-end training, which is how all modern autonomous vehicles learn to drive. We built the radar hardware and radar simulator to change that.

<https://youtu.be/gxdcpLKO_xA>

Today, a robotaxi costs hundreds of thousands of dollars, largely because it relies on lidar, an expensive sensor that works but doesn't scale. **Radar costs tens of dollars per unit, is already in 90% of US cars**, and works in rain, snow, fog, and dust where lidar and cameras degrade. The problem is that no one has built a radar that is compatible with how autonomous vehicles are actually trained.

**The state of the art in autonomy is end-to-end training:** a single neural network learns driving actions directly from raw sensor data. Inclusion in end-to-end training requires two things from each sensor: access to raw data and a high-fidelity simulator. Cameras have both. Lidars have both. Radars have neither. Every automotive radar on the market throws away over 99% of the raw data before the model sees it, and no existing world model is able to simulate radar data.

**Self-driving requires multi-sensor redundancy** and depth sensing that cameras alone cannot provide, but camera-radar fusion can. An OEM that adopts Congruent's radar can train a single end-to-end system on several cameras and radars together, reaching full self-driving, at a sensor cost low enough to ship in every vehicle they make.

We are Clement Barthes and Evan Carnahan, two PhDs who met as research engineers building radar perception pipelines for autonomous vehicles. Clement earned his doctorate in Structural Mechanics from UC Berkeley and developed advanced sensor systems for automotive and structural health monitoring applications. Strength training is gaining traction in both the longevity community and academia, where growing evidence links muscle mass and strength to lower all-cause mortality — yet existing wearables are failing to deliver a seamless strength tracking experience. Fort is **building a screenless wearable that detects strength training and fatigue** while also tracking sleep, cardio, and overall health in an all-day worn device.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98029&key=user_uploads/3343572/6f0f58e4-335c-4f2b-b2b0-bb098aa6cde3)

**Co-founder Story**: My name is Zac. I met Miranda at a squat rack in Fitness SF - a little over a year later we got engaged. I met Paul in university where we designed, built, and raced electric vehicles. Paul and I worked at Tesla for the next 4-5 yrs doing much of the same. I introduced Miranda to Paul in late 2024, knowing that he wanted to work on something new, and Fort was born. I worked on the nights/weekends with Miranda and Paul prototyping designs until Fort occupied most of my mind share, joining full time in December ‘25.

We have a tight knit team that has experience shipping hardware at scale and a strong belief that (1) improving human health is the greatest technological frontier in the age of AI and (2) consumer devices will have a meaningful impact in people’s wellness.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98029&key=user_uploads/3343572/a1b5506e-26b6-4b5b-bd45-a33ad15c50c8)

Whether you are wearing it in the gym or out to dinner, we want it to be something that you actually want to wear and blend seamlessly with other jewelry but be lightweight enough to wear in the gym.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98029&key=user_uploads/3343572/197389c4-4d80-448e-9c16-8999c0029a64)

In addition to detailed strength data, the Fort App also features insights into cardio, stress, and sleep, showing how they are all interconnected: “Learn how your lifestyle affects your strength, and what metrics move the needle on your strength progress”.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98029&key=user_uploads/3343572/7c19300b-5953-4a8b-8a17-db1663fb8553)

For a limited time, pre-order sales are discounted to $289 to the general public (starting $349) which includes the production device + 1 year of software. This discounted pre-order campaign will be capped at 1,000 pre-orders before we move to MSRP - [**https://www.fort.cx/#pricing**](https://www.fort.cx/#pricing)**.**

launches.title: Return Signals - proactive high-touch support for e-commerce brands
launches.tagline: AI-powered post-purchase messaging that reduces returns and increases repeat purchases for e-commerce brands.
launches.detail_body:
Hey everyone 👋\
\
We’re [Alejandro](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alejandrozaniolo/) and [Ilya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ilya-x-valmianski/), cofounders at [Return Signals](https://www.returnsignals.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=launch&utm_campaign=yc_launch).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vb90UYmDDEM>\
\
Over $1T in apparel, footwear, and accessories is sold online. $300B of that gets returned. We believe many of these returns are driven by a poor post-purchase customer experience.

This is why we are building an AI-powered luxury concierge that lets brands proactively check in with customers via SMS when their items are delivered.

This high-touch experience drives 5–10% absolute margin uplift while improving CSAT and LTV.

We intelligently recommend appropriate exchanges when customers are unsatisfied. Our texts achieve very high response rates (over 80% of eventual returns), and convert 70% of return intents into exchanges. All this without increasing the combined exchange and return rate.

Because exchanges preserve revenue, our customers retain most of the original sale value.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98031&key=user_uploads/426067/646f2437-889f-46f3-a6e4-ecb5a9eb058a)

We achieve over 95% positive sentiment in our interactions (and almost no negative interactions), with many customers spending multiple messages thanking our bot and developing a personal relationship 🙂

On the backend, we offer comprehensive analytics, including agentic search, which lets brands ask any question and have our AI read through thousands of conversations to find the right answer.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98031&key=user_uploads/426067/536a151f-92a8-4129-bd04-bdb5ed55c023)

**Our backstory**

Alejandro’s family ran two apparel brands in the US (200+ brick-and-mortar stores) that also sell online. Through this, we discovered two things:

1. **The post-purchase customer experience is broken:** brands rarely check in proactively after delivery, which often leads to poor customer experiences, churn, or refunds. Most communication is limited to order tracking, upsells (“get 25% off”), or review requests. There is rarely a true high-touch experience.
2. **Returns are a major pain point for e-commerce brands:** in the retail industry, returns are \~25%, and reducing them directly impacts absolute margin. This is a significant problem for brands.

Ilya is a 2nd-time founder with deep expertise in building conversational systems, including leading the development of the largest US clinically deployed patient-facing chatbot. As somebody who buys almost all of his clothes online, he’s been flabbergasted by how bad the support experience has been, even with AI assistants like Amazon Rufus. There has to be a better way, and that’s why we decided to build Return Signals.

**Our ask**

* If you have contacts at e-commerce brands (e.g., Shopify merchants) with high return rates in categories such as apparel, footwear, accessories, etc., we would greatly appreciate an intro!
* If you or someone you know has experience in retail e-commerce customer service or has felt the pain of high returns, we’d love to speak with them.

Reach out at [alejandro@returnsignals.com](mailto:alejandro@returnsignals.com) and  [ilya@returnsignals.com](mailto:ilya@returnsignals.com)!

launches.title: Cozmo AI: The system of work for enterprises in financial services and insurance
launches.tagline: Multimodal AI employees that see, speak, think and run operations
launches.detail_body:
Hey everyone, we’re [Nuha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nuhahashem/) and [Alok](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alokhk/) from [Cozmo AI](https://cozmox.ai?utm_source=yc-launch&utm_medium=listing&utm_campaign=launch).

**TL;DR** 

We help banks, insurers and lenders deploy multimodal AI employees that interpret documents and videos, speak with customers in real time, think using your policies and do the work in your core systems.

Check out our [launch video](https://youtu.be/IGypdMioyIo).

**❌ The problem**

If you’ve ever seen how a real customer operation gets handled inside a large company, you’ll notice the conversation is usually the shortest part. Most of the time goes into opening 6-10 tools, finding history, checking documents, verifying details and recording what happened afterwards.

We ran into such issues while building a fintech product and spending months embedded with support and operations teams. A support case that looked “simple” from the outside often meant 40 minutes of prep and follow-up wrapped around an 8-minute customer interaction. The work was more around moving data and decisions across messy systems than actually talking to customers.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98015&key=user_uploads/714894/df0f9156-23c1-46c6-b05f-93060b590053)

To handle these cases, we built an internal system that could understand a case end-to-end and take actions across systems automatically. During a demo, a partner stopped us and asked for that system instead of the fintech product itself.

That became Cozmo.

**✅ How Cozmo is solving it**

Cozmo is a system of work for complex enterprise operations, starting with financial services and insurance. Companies use Cozmo to build and deploy AI employees, which are a collection of agents that own workflows end to end. They talk to customers, read documents, interpret videos, apply company policies and update systems like Guidewire, Temenos and Salesforce, pulling humans into the loop only when real judgment or escalation is needed.

Every decision the AI employee makes is logged, including its reasoning and policy reference, providing a complete audit trail for compliance and operations without additional manual effort. This is managed by our proprietary Agent Protocol Engine (APE), the control layer that keeps shared context, enforces policy and ensures every step is tracked for regulated industries.

Cozmo is live with 10+ enterprises, including Fortune Global 500s like Nestlé, and has already handled over 1M production calls and 10M interactions; cutting costs by up to 70% and turning roughly 1 in 13 conversations into revenue.

[Watch Cozmo in action.](https://youtu.be/ek8eE1bXOnU)

**🧬 What’s unique about Cozmo**

Most AI tools are just prompt trees with a UI. They’re fine for neat, repetitive tasks; but they fall apart the moment operations get messy, ending in half‑filled tickets, off‑script collection calls and disputes scattered across systems.

Cozmo is built for that mess:

* **Multimodal by default:** One platform to spin up AI employees that handle inbound and outbound calls, read PDFs and scanned forms, understand video and talk to customers in a single, continuous flow.
* **Runs on intent, not prompts:** You give it responsibilities and policies like a new hire, instead of maintaining endless prompt chains. As new case patterns appear, the AI employee adapts behavior without you rewriting a graph of scripts.
* **APE-powered coordination:** A single Cozmo “employee” is actually a coordinated team of agents, driven by our Agent Protocol Engine (APE), running an internal loop: planning, delegating, checking and rechecking across systems until the case is closed, not just until a workflow box is ticked.

So instead of a scripted bot, you get something that behaves much closer to a high‑performing operations hire: it keeps context, chases down loose ends and keeps pushing the work forward without you needing to orchestrate every move.

**🚀 Our story**

Nuha and Alok have been friends for over 11 years. We scaled a regulated fintech together in Dubai, navigating one of the most demanding regulatory environments in the world. When the regulations and market changed, we were forced to shut it down. We built AI employees to manage the fintech ourselves on cockroach mode, handling communications and documentation across every affected account. 

That system worked, and when a partner saw it, they asked to buy it instead. So we moved from Dubai to San Francisco to build Cozmo. 

Three years, two countries, 180 pivot, and we’re still going.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98015&key=user_uploads/714894/4501b459-03fa-4135-9389-d407946bd5ec)

 🎯 **Our Ask**

We’re onboarding new enterprise customers in financial services and insurance. If you (or someone you know) run claims, collections or large-scale operations at a bank or insurer, we’d love to connect.

launches.title: Beyond Reach Labs: Solar Panels in Space the size of football-fields
launches.tagline: The future in Space is unfolding
launches.detail_body:
**TL;DR** We’re building deployable solar arrays that expand from the size of a dining table to a football field in orbit. We already have several LOIs from Space companies totaling over $175M and are planning our first in-space demo flight for Q2 2027.

<https://youtu.be/j3FkauBHD8o>

# _The Problem:_

Just like the trunk of your car on a road trip, a rocket ride to space is volume-constrained.

But the critical systems that enable Space services — solar arrays and thermal radiators — get better as they get bigger. Power generation and heat dissipation both require a large surface area, and both must be tightly packed for launch.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97994&key=user_uploads/3155260/61659d57-59a7-45a9-bb77-aada242bc186)

As space infrastructure scales, power demands per launch are rising fast. That means more watts generated and rejected. Existing deployable structures don’t scale to meet this demand - they’re unreliable, too expensive, take up too much volume, and, importantly for controlling the satellite, too flimsy after deployment.

Power generation and heat dissipation are becoming the limiting factors for larger, more capable spacecraft.

# _The Solution:_

Beyond Reach Labs builds solar panels and thermal radiators for space that grow from the size of a dining table to a football field in orbit, supporting the growing demand for power from orbital data centers, commercial space stations, and lunar outposts.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97994&key=user_uploads/3155260/d99b0409-8374-4f34-abab-4d7c6de81717)

Our **patented deployable structures** dramatically improve both stowage efficiency and structural stiffness, enabling kilometer-scale systems from a single launch.

We’re starting with deployable solar arrays, where we’ve already secured several multi-million dollar LOIs from customers building next-generation space platforms.

Our first flight demonstration is targeted for late Q2 2027.

# _Why now?_

Power demand in orbit is exploding… scaling from \~**50 Megawatts today to >500 Gigawatts by 2035** (a 10,000x increase), driven by mega-constellations and in-space data centers - and the deployment bottleneck is becoming critical.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97994&key=user_uploads/3155260/15ea5164-dec9-48a4-a7b9-c29861dde096)

# _Why us?_

**Pele Collins:** \~7 years at SpaceX leading parachute engineering & production, supporting 30+ Dragon missions — designing, qualifying, and flying mission-critical space hardware.

**Dr. Mitchell Fogelson:** PhD from Carnegie Mellon focused on the design, optimization, and simulation of large deployable space structures with NASA - and the inventor of BRL’s core technology.

We’ve been building together since freshman year at UPenn (2013).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97994&key=user_uploads/3155260/adf86f6f-da51-46d2-a2bb-e5360ca6037f)

# Long-term vision

Near-term: Make deployables boring, trustworthy, and scalable for today’s missions.

Long-term: Enable kilometer-scale space infrastructure — including artificial-gravity stations and persistent human presence in space.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97994&key=user_uploads/3155260/a3ea1c41-9f88-4a88-b78e-4b78f2d8a543)

If this resonates, please reach out to us here: [founders@beyondreachlabs.io](mailto:founders@beyondreachlabs.io)

# **Links**

Website: <https://www.beyondreachlabs.com>

Pele: <https://www.linkedin.com/in/pelecollins/>

Mitch: <https://www.linkedin.com/in/mitchell-fogelson/>
